theDIVERGENCEHUNT.empirical: 404547 text-key pairs tested for divergence between the two orders, drawn from an exhaustive enumeration over an alphabet spanning ASCII, Latin-1 (U+00E9), BMP CJK (U+4E2D) and a supplementary-plane code point (U+10000), plus 4000 random keys of length 0 to 300 bytes chosen to cross the 23/24 and 255/256 header-bucket boundaries. DIVERGENCES: 0.
theDIVERGENCEHUNT.analytic: The equality is provable, not merely unobserved. For definite-length minimal-header text strings the header f(n) is a bytewise strictly increasing function of the content length n: within a bucket the headers are equal-length big-endian arguments, and across buckets the initial byte takes 0x60+n, 0x78, 0x79, 0x7a, 0x7b in increasing bucket order, so f(n) < f(m) bytewise whenever n < m, and no f(n) is a prefix of any f(m). Since headers are compared first and differ whenever lengths differ, bytewise comparison of encodings decides by length first and content second -- which is the mapOrder sentence. And the encoded length n + h(n) is strictly increasing in n, so mapOrder's own primary key is injective on content length. The two orders are therefore the SAME total order on this domain.

theJcsHazard.measured: CONFIRMED, and I did not take the artifact's word for it. Three separately parameterised flips covering the three stated JCS differences each fail 0 of 7: UTF-16 code-unit key ordering, absence of NFC treatment, and float tolerance. ECMAScript number serialisation is indistinguishable here because every pinned integer is a positive integer far below 2^53.
theJcsHazard.consequence: The doNotDoThis warning is well founded and is the most operationally important sentence in the artifact. A green 7-of-7 suite certifies nothing about which of the two functions was implemented, and the whole difference lives in the vector-untested region. An implementer who reads only the vectors and reaches for RFC 8785 will pass every test in the corpus and be wrong at the first non-ASCII key or first NFD string.

Under the artifact's OWN statusVocabulary -- 'VECTOR-FORCED: at least one named pinned vector fails under at least one named plausible alternative to the rule' -- the encoder-level clause does not qualify: a float-tolerant encoder reproduces 7 of 7, and the three cited fixtures pin a rejection outcome with no digest, so no encoder behaviour can make them pass or fail.
advisories.theInternalINCONSISTENCY: CJ-R11 (duplicate keys) and CJ-R13 (non-string keys) are also rejection rules and are graded PROSE-STATED-VECTOR-UNTESTED for exactly this reason, stated in CJ-R11's own words: 'a rejection rule admits no positive golden vector'. CJ-R12 is the third rejection rule and is graded one notch stronger. There is a genuine evidentiary difference -- R12's rejection IS pinned by named fixtures where R11's and R13's are not -- but the artifact's three-value vocabulary has no slot for it and chose the stronger of the two available.
advisories.theArtifactCONTAINSTHEEVIDENCEAGAINSTITS: CJ-R12's statusScope already says 'the encoder-level rejection is unreachable for admitted values'. The scope note is right; the label above it is not.
advisories.whyItIsNotABlocker: The rule TEXT is byte-verbatim from v4's dataModel and is correct. No implementer who obeys CJ-R12 produces a wrong byte. The defect is that a reader auditing the artifact's evidence base would credit this rule with vector backing it does not have at the encoder -- which matters precisely because this is the rule that carries freeze 6 law 18 into the encoding layer.
advisories.suggestedRepair: either add a fourth status such as REJECTION-PINNED-AT-ADMISSION, or regrade CJ-R12 to PROSE-STATED-VECTOR-UNTESTED with the three fixtures retained as admission-boundary corroboration. Do not weaken the rule.

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- a census sentence quantified one scope too wide
advisories.what: CJ-R04's statusScope states: 'no zero and no negative integer occurs anywhere in the six families' positive vectors.' Measured independently, that is FALSE for zero. FACT-ID-V1's positive vector fact-id-v1-typescript-declares commits anchors[0].startByte = 0 inside preimage tag 14, encoded as 03 0000000000000000 and byte-pinned at 940 preimage bytes and fact:sha256:3e03d85a3782f4938182eaa5e850a9a84311107b6ed9d9855eccaa52803ba59e. The R-1 source vector behind the PDD family also carries zeros, though none of them reaches the committed record.

measuredIntegerCensusByFamily.POLICY-DERIVATION-DIGEST-V1: 0 and 1 in the source vector; no integer reaches the R-B record, whose fields are all text
measuredIntegerCensusByFamily.unionMaximum: 1048576, so the companion claim in UR-2 that 'the largest exercised magnitude is 1048576' is TRUE across all six families

advisories.whyTheCONCLUSIONSURVIVES: The zero that exists is committed through CVE1 as 03 || u64be(0), not through opensip-canonical-json-v1. It constrains the CVE1 zero encoding and says nothing whatever about the JSON profile's decimal spelling of zero. So UR-2 remains correctly UNDETERMINED and CJ-R04's grade is unaffected. The error is in a supporting sentence, and it errs by claiming LESS evidence exists than does -- the conservative direction for an UNDETERMINED verdict, which is why it could not have produced a wrong rule.
advisories.whyItIsSTILLWORTHRECORDING: This is freeze 7.2.2's SCOPING failure mode in miniature -- a claim quantified over a region wider than the one measured -- in a file whose entire value is that its measurements are true. A reader who trusts this sentence and then needs the CVE1 zero spelling will look for evidence the artifact told them does not exist.
advisories.suggestedRepair: narrow the sentence to 'no zero and no negative integer occurs in any of the seven planIntentCommitment fixtures', and optionally add that the CVE1 zero encoding IS forced, by FACT-ID-V1's committed anchors.

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- a verbatim claim that is not verbatim
advisories.what: theRecoveredFunction.dataModel reads 'JSON objects, arrays, strings, booleans, signed integers and null ONLY. Floating-point numbers are forbidden. (Verbatim from the primary prose source.)' The source at c2-plan-stage-schema.v4#planIntent.canonicalCommitment.encoding.dataModel reads 'JSON objects, arrays, strings, booleans, signed integers and null only; floating-point numbers are forbidden.' The rendering capitalises 'only' and replaces the semicolon with a full stop and a capital F.
advisories.checkedProperly: byte-literal, whitespace-folded, markdown-folded and case-insensitive comparisons all return NOT IDENTICAL. This is not a freeze 7.7 false negative.
advisories.theCorpusPRECEDENT: plan-and-policy-identity-recipes.v1#planIdField3Resolution refuses to call a quotation verbatim for a smaller alteration than this: 'NOT called verbatim, because it is not: the source carries backticks and line breaks this rendering removes.' The standard exists in this corpus and this line falls below it.
advisories.materiality: The meaning is unchanged and no rule moves. It matters because freeze 7.7's stated property is that in this corpus formatting is semantics, and because a reviewer who spot-checks one 'verbatim' claim and finds it re-cased has to re-check every other quotation. I did re-check them: every other quotation the artifact makes -- fourteen tested across five source artifacts -- is byte-exact.
advisories.suggestedRepair: either restore the source punctuation and casing, or drop the parenthetical to 'Stated at the primary prose source.'

advisories.grade: ADVISORY -- a paraphrase that softens a rejection rule
advisories.what: siblingEncodings.CVE1.constraints renders the normative source's 'declared sets are sorted and duplicates rejected before CVE1 encoding' as 'the set is sorted and deduplicated BEFORE encoding'.
advisories.why: 'Deduplicated' means silently drop; 'duplicates rejected' means refuse the input. They are different behaviours producing different outcomes on the same input, and the whole discipline this artifact recovers is reject-do-not-normalise -- a distinction it states carefully at CJ-R10, CJ-R11, UR-3 and in recordFramingSuite.textComponent. A reader implementing set fields from this sentence would silently mint an identity for a manifest the owning surface refuses.
advisories.materiality: No pinned vector exercises a duplicate inside a declared set, so no digest in the index moves. The defect is entirely forward-looking.

observations.what: reproductionLog.results.flipBattery's '11 alternative-rule encoders' is not recomputable from the artifact's bytes; 14 alternatives are named, 13 distinct. A process self-report, not a measurement.
observations.generalForm: freeze 7.2.2's rider on self-certifying artifacts applies to the whole reproductionLog: it records properties a reviewer can re-derive but cannot verify were derived by the author. That bound is inherent and the artifact does not overclaim around it. In this instance the bound is discharged, because this review re-derived every figure in it independently.

Also, delivery.v3 and delivery.v4 both derive from delivery.v2 -- they are SIBLINGS, not a chain, which DR-2's phrase 'the v4 successor' could be read as denying.

observations.aLIMITOFMYOWNINSTRUMENT: my resolver reported 2 operation errors on delivery.v5, both from a path grammar that does not parse bracket indices such as declaredUnresolvedDependencies.entries[6]. Neither failed operation touches capabilityManifestIdentity, so the DCM reading above is unaffected. This is a limit of my resolver, not a claim about delivery.v5. The artifact claims 0 resolve errors only on c2 v10 and delivery.v3 and v4, and I confirm 0 on all three.

observations.what: The artifact's jxCanonExcluded warning is correct and I verified the specific defect it cites. Resolved c2 v10's documentIdentityEncoding.productions.number reads 'FRAME(n, the shortest decimal string that round-trips to the same IEEE-754 binary64 value)'; v11 operation 2 replaces it with a production that additionally requires a decimal point or exponent. Under v10's rule the value 1.0 renders as FRAME('n','1') = n1:1; under v11's as n3:1.0. That is exactly the n1:1 versus n3:1.0 defect named.
observations.whyItMATTERS: opensip-jx-canon-v1 has an IEEE-754 binary64 number production. opensip-canonical-json-v1 forbids floating point outright. Two JSON-adjacent canonicalisations, one surface, opposite number models. The artifact naming this solely so no reader conflates them is a real service and the conflation would be silent.

observations.what: A third statement of the CBOR map order exists and is not cited: fact-plane.v1#factRecordContractV1.relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1.canonicalPayloadEncoding.mapOrder reads 'ascending unsigned lexicographic order of each key's deterministic-CBOR bytes'. It agrees with the RFC 8949 reading, and it sits in the surface that owns the FACT-ID vectors the resolution is measured against. Citing it would have made liveContradictionConfronted stronger at zero cost.

The subject's POLICY-DERIVATION family source line names 'the R-1 head (r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.6#policyDerivationIdentity)'. Two things measured against that phrase. First, r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.7.json now exists -- written DURING this review, see reviewConditions -- and derives from v1.6 with 28 operations, 15 of which touch policyDerivationIdentity. v1.6 is no longer the head. Second, v1.6's own top-level status reads CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, which sits awkwardly beside the subject's phrase 'the R-B recipe was applied into the R-1 head'.
observations.theCHARITABLEREADINGISPROBABLYRIGHT: 'Applied into' most naturally means 'carried into that document's own bytes', which is true: v1.6 does carry a policyDerivationIdentity block with its own recipe, primitives, preimage and record grammar. The subject also labels the whole family 'CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED lineage' in the same sentence, so it is not claiming binding status for anything.
observations.impact: ZERO on any published value. Measured: 0 of the subject's 17 indexed digests appear in v1.6 or v1.7. The 17 come from plan-and-policy-identity-recipes.v1, which is unchanged and which I reproduced in full.
observations.grade: OBSERVATION. Same class as O-2: a head-naming that is one version stale while every digest under it remains correct. Worth a one-word edit ('carried into' rather than 'applied into', and a version bump on the reference) in whatever successor repairs the four advisories.
observations.aGENERALPOINTWORTHKEEPING: Two of this review's five observations are stale head references (delivery.v4 and r1 v1.6), and one of them went stale WHILE THE REVIEW WAS RUNNING. In a corpus where heads advance faster than reviews complete, a recovery artifact that names heads by version acquires staleness it cannot prevent. Naming heads BY DIGEST, as freeze 7.2 already requires of reviews, would make each such reference self-dating: a reader could tell at a glance whether the reference had moved. That is a cheap structural improvement and it is not a criticism of this author's diligence.

closingAssessment.isThisRECOVERYORDESIGN: RECOVERY. The test that settles it is that every rule's citation resolves to text that exists at the cited path, and that the artifact's failure direction throughout is understatement. It declines to promote UR-5 from an implication it explicitly identifies as sound. It grades CJ-R08 untested despite holding a forcing vector for one of its clauses. It refuses to select between the two CBOR readings even after proving they coincide on the whole reachable domain. It leaves the NFC divergence between the JSON encoder and every sibling standing rather than harmonising it. Four separate opportunities to smuggle a decision in under a recovered heading, four refusals. The one place it reaches beyond its evidence is a status LABEL on a rule whose text it quoted correctly.
closingAssessment.whatTheNUMBERMEANS: 41 of 41 indexed vectors, plus 13 extras, plus 4 worked examples, plus 14 of 14 published flip counts, plus 13 of 13 self-census rows, reproduced by programs sharing no code with the corpus or with the author. The dispatch said that number is the artifact's actual worth. It is 41 of 41.
closingAssessment.theRESIDUALRISK: It is not in this file. It is that this file BINDS NOTHING while opensip-canonical-json-v1 is invoked as a function underneath planIntentCommitment, PLAN-ID-V1 field 13, and every JSON-canonicalising identity recipe in the corpus, defined nowhere else as a specification. The five UNDETERMINED entries are real gaps in the corpus, not gaps in this recovery, and they will be discovered by the first implementation that disagrees rather than by any vector that exists today. UR-1, UR-3 and UR-4 in particular are each one non-ASCII key, one NFD string or one embedded quote away from producing two different PlanIds from one PlanIntent.
closingAssessment.recommendation: Repair the four advisories -- all are single-sentence edits requiring a version bump under freeze 7.2, since the reviewed bytes may not be edited in place -- and take the five settling vectors to the surfaces that own them. The recovery itself needs nothing.
